- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–3 days); cap forecast peak at 2–3% above recent high.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate in periods of high volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is mixed or trending sideways.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/0.67 alternation, model often misreads momentum; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
